prompt:
Let $P,Q,R$ be classical propositions, with $\equiv$ meaning equal truth values under every assignment. Which law names this pattern?
$P\land(P\lor Q)\equiv P$

answers.explanation: If the repeated proposition is false, the whole conjunction is false; if it is true, the inner disjunction is true. The other proposition therefore cannot affect the result.
Applying negation twice restores the original truth value. That is a different pattern from the displayed law.
Moving negation through a conjunction negates both operands and changes conjunction to disjunction. That is a different pattern from the displayed law.
A proposition and its negation cover both possible truth values. That is a different pattern from the displayed law.
The two operands exchange places while the connective stays the same. That is a different pattern from the displayed law.
Only the grouping changes; the order of the operands and the connective stay fixed. That is a different pattern from the displayed law.
Disjunction distributes over conjunction, repeating the outside operand in both resulting disjunctions. That is a different pattern from the displayed law.
A neutral constant leaves the other operand unchanged. That is a different pattern from the displayed law.
An absorbing constant fixes the result regardless of the other operand. That is a different pattern from the displayed law.
Combining a proposition with itself using conjunction adds no new requirement. That is a different pattern from the displayed law.
